concepts.def: Form where soft rock erodes faster than hard rock along the coast.
Sequence: crack, cave, arch, stack, stump on a headland.
Flat rocky shelf left as a cliff retreats from undercutting.
Deposit of sand or shingle between high and low tide marks.
Long, narrow ridge of sediment growing into the sea from land.
Famous UK spit at the mouth of the Humber Estuary. 🏖

walkthroughs.body_html:
Discordant coasts have alternating rock bands.

Soft rock erodes quickly to form bays; hard rock juts out as headlands.

Different rates of erosion sculpt the shoreline.

walkthroughs.h2: On a headland, waves attack cracks.
walkthroughs.body_html:
On a headland, waves attack cracks.

Crack to cave; cave through to other side becomes an arch.

The arch collapses to leave a stack; stack erodes to a stump.

walkthroughs.h2: Where the coastline bends, longshore drift carries sediment
walkthroughs.body_html:
Where the coastline bends, longshore drift carries sediment into open water.

The deposit grows out as a spit, often with a hooked end shaped by changing winds.

Example: Spurn Head at the Humber mouth.
